context: Emit an informational lint line for exempt-category items (e.g. 'falsifiability check skipped: category flake') so exemptions are auditable. Do NOT add a category enum - corpus evidence kills it. Optionally tighten the weak bare-word alternates to phrase-anchored forms; weigh the cost of re-flagging honest 'fails until X' phrasings before doing so.
description: Driven 2026-08-01 on a scratch DB: an item created with --category flake and a rung whose expected reads 'always passes' lints clean under lint.require_falsifiable_rung=on. --category is unvalidated free text (the hosted corpus has 170+ distinct values, so an enum would break import losslessness and is not viable). The exemption itself is semantically right for tripwires/acceptance runs; the hole is that it is INVISIBLE - lint output never says an item was exempted, so a wrongly-categorized item skips the check silently. Also observed: bare 'today'/'once'/'until' anywhere in expected text satisfies _GATING_EXPECTED_RE (corpus impact small: 4 open items pass only via weak words, 2 of them honestly gating).
